hero.headline: Vero Beach parents sue city over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed, reburied without consent
hero.teaser: Two Vero Beach parents filed an amended lawsuit alleging their infant son's remains were accidentally disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and reinterred without their knowledge or consent.
hero.body:
Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo's son, identified only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old. According to the complaint, he was buried at Crestlawn Cemetery on Aug. 15, 2007, where his parents believed he had remained undisturbed for nearly 18 years. The lawsuit centers on Crestlawn Cemetery, which is operated by the City of Vero Beach.

The parents allege that sometime between the burial in 2007 and April 2025, maintenance or irrigation work was taking place near the burial site when heavy equipment breached the grave. The lawsuit alleges A.C.'s casket, contents, and remains were damaged or destroyed. According to the complaint, someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket and reinter the child without notifying or obtaining consent from the parents. The lawsuit claims the parents were deprived of the opportunity to participate in laying their son to rest again and were never informed that the burial site had allegedly been disturbed. The parents say they did not learn what allegedly happened until April 2025. The lawsuit does not explain how they became aware of the alleged disturbance.

The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment. The lawsuit also alleges the city failed to protect the burial site and failed to follow Florida laws and administrative rules governing cemetery maintenance, disinterment and the handling of human remains. "The Defendant's conduct is outrageous and goes beyond all bounds of decency in a civilized society, is not dignified and is intolerable," the complaint states.

This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false. Instead, the court ruled the legal claims, as originally pleaded, could not proceed against the city under Florida law. The City of Vero Beach declined to comment on the newly filed amended complaint. However, in court filings responding to the original lawsuit, the city disputed the parents' allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage. The city's attorney submitted a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher shot and killed; family member arrested in connection with death
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce community is mourning the loss of Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Es.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce community is mourning the loss of Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind 3 adult children. His family released a statement about his death, saying they are sad to report the loss of their dad to a senseless act of violence and asking people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online discussing any other details as this is still an active investigation.

Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as more than just an educator. Coleman said Barnes was really a pillar of the community and that she and friends who didn't grow up with dads looked at him as a father figure. Coleman, now 37 years old, said Barnes made an impact on them life-long and that the fact she kept communication with him from 7th grade, well before social media came around, says a lot about his character. Coleman and others are calling for justice as the homicide investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Indian River County Sheriff releases details after 2 bodies found near Sebastian
cards.teaser: Sheriff Eric Flowers said Thursday there is no connection between two men whose bodies were found in the same area this week near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released new details Thursday after two bodies were found in the same area this week. Sheriff Eric Flowers said at this point there is no connection between the two men, one found on Monday and the other on Wednesday. On Monday, the body of James Thompson, 44, was found on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. An autopsy is pending in that case.

On Wednesday, shortly after 4 p.m., a second body, which was heavily decomposed, was located in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian. This body was found just across the street from Monday's location. The sheriff's office said Wednesday the man has been identified and detectives were working on notifying next of kin. Investigators have not determined whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. The sheriff's office said Wednesday in a statement that it understands two death investigations in close proximity may raise concern in the community. Anyone with information in either of these cases is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.

cards.headline: Sheriff says no connection between 2 bodies found near Sebastian this week
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released new details Thursday after two bodies were found in the same area this week. Sheriff Eric Flowers said at this point there is no connection between the two men, one found on Monday and the other on Wednesday.

On Monday, the body of James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident, was found on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. The sheriff said Thompson had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian and was last seen on Sunday walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1 around 1:30 p.m. "This gentleman has a history of fentanyl use. He has a history of mental health issues," Flowers said. "On the third of July, he made a purchase of methamphetamine. He had gone into a manic state." Flowers said Thompson had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County "many times." An autopsy is pending in that case.

On Wednesday, shortly after 4 p.m., a second body, which was heavily decomposed, was located in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian. This body was found just across the street from Monday's location. The sheriff's office said Wednesday the man has been identified and detectives were working on notifying next of kin.

The sheriff's office said Wednesday that investigators have not determined whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. "We understand two death investigations in close proximity may raise concern in the community," the sheriff's office said Wednesday in a statement. Anyone with information in either of these cases is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.

cards.headline: Dale Mincey held on felony warrants after shooting death of Fort Pierce man
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office identified Dale Mincey, 41, as the suspect in a shooting that killed Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Deputies responded to a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive at around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim was identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. The suspect in the homicide investigation has been identified as Dale A. Mincey by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie Public Schools. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. The sheriff's office said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95 in St. Lucie County faces pushback from neighbors
cards.body:
A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but neighbors are pushing back against the project they say will eliminate the area's rural character. County planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace on June 18. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August for the project called Indrio Town Center, which would bring 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space to land near Interstate 95. The development area is equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches.

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, representing property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will include open green space and an over 26-acre park. Heinzelmann said the design incorporates a lot of open space and keeps a native buffer along Indrio Road. The project aims to bring a mix of commercial and retail space, and possibly residential units, to the area.

Susan Lewis, who has lived near the proposed site for 15 years and runs a farm rescue on property that has been in her family for decades, said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. Lewis said she has dogs and horses that have 10 acres to run around, but worries that space is gone if the development proceeds. She told WPTV she believes there are plenty of other places for developers to build. Lewis said she moved to the area to be in the wilderness and preserve what Florida used to look like, and the development would transform that rural landscape.

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. The overlay district allows for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character and maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities, according to Benton. She said the district allows development that considers compatibility and integration into the county's need for infrastructure, quality of life, jobs and connectivity to the interstate and roadway system. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Three lawsuits challenge Florida property tax amendment before November vote
cards.teaser: Three separate legal challenges now target Amendment Three, a constitutional amendment placed on the November ballot by state lawmakers that would expand homestead property tax exemptions.
cards.body:
Florida's property tax amendment backed by the state Legislature is now facing a growing legal fight, with three lawsuits challenging whether the ballot language gives voters a fair explanation or a political sales pitch. The lawsuits target Amendment Three, which was placed on the November ballot by state lawmakers. Three separate legal challenges have been filed by nonprofit Save Our Voters, former South Miami Mayor Philip Stoddard, and former lawmakers Jeff Brandes and Al Lawson. Attorney Jamie Cole, who filed the first lawsuit, said the cases are expected to be consolidated, with a hearing currently set for July 29. The lawsuits take aim at several phrases in the ballot summary, including language saying the amendment would save homes from excessive property taxes, protect small businesses, ensure funding for core services, and ensure fairness for Florida residents. Plaintiffs argue those phrases are campaign-style language urging voters to support it rather than a neutral explanation.

If approved by 60% of voters, the measure would expand non-school homestead property tax exemptions, eventually exempting up to $250,000 of a homestead's value by 2028. It would also limit some future assessment increases on non-homestead property and place new restrictions on how local governments use property tax dollars. State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, said following approval of the measure in early June that relief is coming and money would be put back in the pockets of Floridians, provided the amendment receives a 60% vote. Ron DeSantis said he will vote for the amendment but does not plan to lead the campaign. He said he does not think voters will see him leading on this particular proposal because it is not all that he was hoping to see. If a judge agrees the ballot language is misleading, the Florida Attorney General could be tasked with rewriting the summary.

cards.headline: Jensen Beach gym holds fundraiser workout for family of 5-year-old killed in bike accident
cards.teaser: Orangetheory Fitness in Jensen Beach is raising funds for the family of Garrett Leonard, a 5-year-old who was killed in a bicycle accident at a motocross park in Miami.
cards.body:
A Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness is raising funds for the family of Garrett Leonard, a 5-year-old boy who was killed in an accident. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office says the 5-year-old was riding a bicycle in between vehicles at a motocross park in Miami and was hit when he crossed the path of a pick-up truck. MDSO says the driver cooperated in the investigation. They told WPTV on Wednesday that no charges had been filed in the case. His family was not ready to provide a statement Wednesday but shared photos.

Orangetheory coach Shelby Collier said she and gym owner Tabitha Lavery learned of the tragedy that struck two of their members and didn't hesitate to act. Lavery described the couple as valued members of the community. Collier reflected on the pride Garrett's father showed for his son, saying he would say "This is Garrett, look what he did, look what he did, and just the proudest dad." Lavery said they put together a 90-minute fundraiser workout to help them get through this hard time. All of the proceeds will go toward a GoFundMe started to ease the financial burden that comes with losing a loved one. The workout is this Sunday and is open to the public.

hero.headline: Park Vista Cobras football team sets sights on state playoffs after strong finish to 2025 season
hero.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games.

"Felt good throughout the second half of that season," senior Harris Bender said. "We're just working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, like you said, and we have all the pieces in place now, it's just about executing." The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna emphasized the importance of taking the season one step at a time. "We got to take it one game at a time," Hanna said. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs." Senior Erik Lee echoed that sentiment, noting the team has the talent necessary for success but must be willing to work for it. "Coming in, I feel like we got the guys that we need to get it done," Lee said. "But also, we got to put the work in to get there as well."

Senior Justice Jones expressed confidence about the team's prospects for the upcoming season. "It's going to feel amazing, because I already know it's gonna happen, definitely," Jones said. The Cobras are looking to build on their late 2025 success and translate that into a full season of strong performances in 2026.

Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August. The team hopes its improved play from the end of last season will carry over as they pursue their first state playoff appearance and potential championship run since claiming the title in 2017. With returning seniors providing leadership and the coaching staff preaching a game by game approach, the Cobras believe they have the right combination to achieve their goals this fall.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August season debut
cards.teaser: Four teams with names inspired by pioneering women will begin play on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois, marking the return of women's professional baseball.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The league also includes the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters. The WPBL's debut season begins on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March that this is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball, and now for us to actually be with each other, there's so much freedom and peace within it.

The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. Their logo includes graphic lines surrounding a baseball, mimicking the speed of a fastball and resembling the New York skyline. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. Their logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The logo is a capital Q topped with four baseball diamonds. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist. Their logo is an osprey clasping a baseball bat in its talons.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to dramatic 3-2 World Cup comeback victory over Egypt
cards.teaser: Argentina scored three goals in the final 11 minutes to overcome a 2-0 deficit and advance to the World Cup quarterfinals, with Messi scoring his eighth goal of the tournament.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 21st World Cup goal in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2, and Enzo Fernandez netted the winning goal in stoppage time to complete Argentina's improbable 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday. The defending champions trailed by two goals with only 11 minutes of regulation time remaining before Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute. Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, scored his eighth goal of the tournament. The 39-year-old led Argentina to the comeback despite missing a first-half penalty kick that was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir. Messi later hit the post when the score was 1-0, marking his second penalty miss of the tournament after also failing from the spot against Austria in the group stage.

Argentina will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. The team is bidding to become the first to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. Egypt took a surprising lead in the 15th minute when Yasser Ibrahim got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross and head the ball into the bottom corner. Mostafa Zico scored Egypt's second goal in the 67th minute. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said he was so emotional about the group of players.

cards.headline: US men's World Cup match against Belgium sets all-time viewership record with 30 million viewers
cards.teaser: Monday's World Cup match became the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, with viewership peaking at 36 million during the second half of the 4-1 loss.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported. According to Fox, the match drew more than 30 million viewers. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
cards.teaser: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies to end the three-year program that vetted Russians for neutral status at qualifying events.
cards.body:
The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The move was expected since the International Olympic Committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The IOC stands in solidarity with the Olympic community of Ukraine, which the Olympic movement has supported since the beginning of the war, and will continue to do so, the Olympic body said in a statement after a meeting of its executive board.

The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension were imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine. Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem, saying that decision will come at an appropriate time. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal, opening October 31.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The festival is organized by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. and will take place in Vero Beach during November 2026.

The annual event brings seafood vendors, entertainment and family activities to the Treasure Coast each year. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. produces the festival as one of the region's signature food and entertainment gatherings.

No specific dates, venue location or ticket information were announced in the initial festival announcement. Additional details about the November festival are expected to be released by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. in the coming months.

hero.headline: Updated Live Local Act takes effect in Florida, expanding affordable housing opportunities
hero.teaser: Florida's revised Live Local Act became active, expanding affordable housing opportunities across the state while fueling debate at the local level.
hero.body:
Florida's updated Live Local Act took effect today, expanding affordable housing opportunities while fueling local debate across the state. The revised legislation builds on previous affordable housing measures passed by the state Legislature.

The law aims to address Florida's housing affordability crisis by creating additional opportunities for affordable housing development statewide. Local governments and housing advocates continue to debate the implementation and impact of the expanded provisions.

A proposed 85-acre development called Indrio Town Center off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality despite pushback from neighbors who say it will transform the area's rural character. The project would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

Susan Lewis, who has lived near the proposed site for 15 years running a farm rescue on property that has been in her family for decades, said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. Lewis said she has dogs and horses that have 10 acres to run around. The proposed development is 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres, an area equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches. Lewis told reporters she's worried this development will change the rural landscape in St. Lucie County. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do. We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like," said Lewis.

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," said Benton. "It allows for that development very strategically, that considers compatibility and how it's integrated into both the county's need for infrastructure, need for quality of life, jobs, and also connectivity to our interstate and roadway system."

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will include open green space and an over 26-acre park. Heinzelmann said the design incorporates a lot of open space and keeps a native buffer along Indrio Road. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Barnes killed in shooting; family member arrested
cards.teaser: Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher at West Gate K-8 in Fort Pierce, was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in For.
cards.body:
Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children. His family released a statement asking people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online as the investigation continues.

Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as more than just an educator. Coleman said Barnes was really a pillar of the community and served as a father figure to students who didn't grow up with dads. Coleman, now 37 years old, said she and Barnes kept communication since she was in 7th grade, well before social media came around. Coleman and others are calling for justice as the homicide investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Dale Mincey held on felony warrants after shooting death of Fort Pierce man
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office identified Dale Mincey, 41, as the suspect in a shooting that killed Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Deputies responded to a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive at around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim was identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. The suspect in the homicide investigation has been identified as Dale A. Mincey by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie Public Schools. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. The sheriff's office said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Manager Releases Proposed FY 2026-27 Budget
cards.teaser:

cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The proposed budget represents a 12.12% increase from the current fiscal year, which the city says is driven by inflation and capital projects. The general fund budget is proposed at about $230.6 million, an 8.48% increase, or roughly $18 million more than FY 2025-26.

The city's taxable value is also expected to rise. According to the budget brief, Port St. Lucie's estimated certified taxable value increased 5.45%, from $25.5 billion in FY 2025-26 to $26.9 billion in FY 2026-27, due to growth and property appreciation.

Under the proposal, the operating millage rate would remain at 4.6607 per $1,000 of taxable value. The total proposed millage rate would remain 4.9750, including the voter-approved Crosstown Parkway debt service millage of 0.3143.

Residents could see some fee changes. The stormwater fee would increase by $6, bringing the residential rate to $195. The solid waste assessment would increase to $482.16 under the city's contract with its solid waste vendor, though qualified residential homeowners would receive a one-time credit of either $364 or $64. The city also proposes a 3.5% increase in the water rate, while the sewer rate would remain unchanged.

The proposed budget also includes long-term infrastructure planning. The city says capital improvement projects over the next five years are projected to cost about $1.069 billion. The largest portion is for utility system upgrades, listed at $672.7 million. Other planned spending includes $51.1 million for Walton & One, Torino & Tradition Regional Parks and O.L. Peacock Park, $34.8 million for facilities maintenance, $24.5 million for street resurfacing and $9.9 million for sidewalk projects.

The budget brief also notes that Port St. Lucie's long-term debt has declined from more than $1.042 billion in FY 2009-10 to a projected $765 million in FY 2026-27, a reduction of 26.58% over 16 years. The proposed budget includes a net increase of seven positions in the Utility Systems Fund, bringing the city to 1,550.25 full-time equivalent positions.

City Council will review the proposed budget during a workshop July 22-23 at the Community Center, located at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.

The workshop will also be televised live on the city's website, Xfinity Channel 20 and Blue Stream Fiber Channel 20.

hero.headline: Sheriff says no connection between 2 bodies found near Sebastian this week
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released new details Thursday after two bodies were found in the same area this week. Sheriff Eric Flowers said at this point there is no connection between the two men, one found on Monday and the other on Wednesday.

On Monday, the body of James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident, was found on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. The sheriff said Thompson had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian and was last seen on Sunday walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1 around 1:30 p.m. "This gentleman has a history of fentanyl use. He has a history of mental health issues," Flowers said. "On the third of July, he made a purchase of methamphetamine. He had gone into a manic state." Flowers said Thompson had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County "many times." An autopsy is pending in that case.

On Wednesday, shortly after 4 p.m., a second body, which was heavily decomposed, was located in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian. This body was found just across the street from Monday's location. The sheriff's office said Wednesday the man has been identified and detectives were working on notifying next of kin.

The sheriff's office said Wednesday that investigators have not determined whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. "We understand two death investigations in close proximity may raise concern in the community," the sheriff's office said Wednesday in a statement. Anyone with information in either of these cases is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.
